- **Rossouw (2015):** re-enchantment as a secularized Christian (theological) project ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-rossouw-aestheology-new-otium-2015/index.md>)).
- **Lotz (2015):** "new spirit of capitalism" talk veils the real restructuring needed ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lotz-marx-and-philosophy-2015/index.md>)).
- **Labelled interpretation:** the book does *not* call for re-sacralization. The Tunis motion explicitly warns against locating spirit only in religion. Its "enchantment" is closer to motivation, desire and meaning sustained by knowledge.

# Economy of contribution (*économie de la contribution*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **economy of contribution**

## Definition (the book's usage)

The economy of contribution is the industrial model proposed to replace the **consumerist** model. Its traits:

1. **No separation between producers and consumers.** There are only *contributors*, as in free/open-source software, Wikipedia, smart grids and community-supported agriculture (AMAP).
2. Its value takes the form of **positive externalities**: care for self and others, and Sen's **capabilities**, much of which cannot be monetized.
3. Its milieus are **associated** (Simondon), so participants individuate themselves by individuating the milieu.
4. It aims at **de-proletarianization**: the reconstitution of *savoir-faire*, *savoir-vivre* and theoretical knowledge.

## Where it appears

- [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>) §3 (named and defined), §6 (free software as de-proletarianization), §7 (generalization: smart grids, AMAP, contributory businesses), §9.3 (fiscal policy for positive externalities; work as distinct from employment). N. 9: the concept was suggested by Franck Cormerais. P. 25: contributory businesses must learn from the failure of the cooperative movements of Charles Gide and Marcel Mauss.
- **Already explicit in 2006:** [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) pp. 36–37 names "the **economy of contribution** typical of open-source software" (Linux; users as practitioners), grounded in the IP network as an associated milieu since 1992. This economy furnishes "the concepts of a new industrial model" called to replace that of dissociated milieus (p. 36). The internet as associated milieu enables an industrial model resting on the association of addressees and addressors, which produces "a new form of sociality and a new spirit of capitalism (while waiting for the replacement of the latter by another form of society)" (p. 37).
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) p. 87: **Wikipedia** is "an extraordinary success" showing that the participatory logic of associated milieus is "an extremely new and powerful dynamic". P. 91 and pp. 92–93: hypertextual "**societies of authors and readers**", with Web 2.0 as infrastructure anticipating "a new industrial model".
- [Motion](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/06-tunis-motion/index.md>) p. 95: knowledge as a common good, with only temporary property limits.

## Related terms

[associated milieu](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/associated-milieu/index.md>) · [proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>) · [care](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/care/index.md>) · [pharmakon](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/pharmakon/index.md>) · [otium/negotium](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/otium-negotium/index.md>) · [short-termism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/short-termism/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** three traits: no producer/consumer split; non-monetizable value as positive externality; an economy of **existences** as much as of subsistences. The contributor is neither consumer, nor taxpayer, nor gift-giver in Mauss's sense ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler–Lemmens interview (2010):** a "new industrial model". Stiegler explicitly brackets whether it will still be capitalism. Lemmens presses him on the marginality of free software and on the neoliberal state ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-lemmens-stiegler-interview-krisis-2011/index.md>)).
- **Hui &amp; Halpin (2013):** a Simondonian design programme for social networks along contributory lines ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hui-halpin-collective-individuation-2013/index.md>)).
- **Abbinnett (2015):** frees labour from "ratio" so that otium becomes a universal good ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-abbinnett-politics-of-spirit-2015/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Manche (2021):** the most rigorous critique. Contribution rests on a teleological, operaist reading of automation. It sidelines profit and accumulation, yields "good vs bad capitalism" reformism, and risks **self-exploitation and co-optation** by corporate partners ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-manche-proletarianisation-not-capitalism-2021/index.md>)).
- **Lemmens (2017):** accepts the pharmacological frame but criticizes Stiegler's **statism** ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-lemmens-digital-pharmakon-general-intellect-2017/index.md>)).
- **Lotz (2015):** the book's only example is Wikipedia (p. 87); Benkler's *Wealth of Networks* says more. Lotz overstates this: Ch. 1 also cites open-source software and Linux (p. 36), and the 2010 Manifesto cites free software, smart grids and AMAP ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lotz-marx-and-philosophy-2015/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler's own revision:** by *The Neganthropocene* (2018) he judged the algorithmic web "a systemically dissociating milieu", which qualifies the 2010 optimism ([Ross](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).

# Grammatization (*grammatisation*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **grammatization**

## Definition

Grammatization is the process by which temporal **flows** (speech, gesture, perception, calculation) are **discretized** into reproducible spatial elements, "grammes". The examples are the alphabet's letters, the machine-tool's encoded gestures, the phonograph groove and binary code. Stiegler takes the term from linguist **Sylvain Auroux** (*La révolution technologique de la grammatisation*, 1994), who used it for the alphabet's precedence over grammar and logic. He generalizes it to the whole of technical history and links it to Derrida's grammatology. Each stage of grammatization creates new possibilities of knowledge and new risks of **proletarianization**. It goes with a **general organology**: the co-evolution of physiological organs, technical organs and social organizations.

## Where it appears

- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) n. 2 defines grammatization as a process of description, formation and discretization of human behaviours that makes their reproducibility possible. §3 (pp. 31–33): critiques of the culture industry lack "a projection into the dynamic of the process of grammatization" and an "organological approach" (note defining *general organology*). The section "Grammatization and individuation—yesterday, today, and tomorrow" (pp. 47–51; translated earlier by Barker, [source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-barker-new-formations-2012/index.md>)) gives the deep history: hydraulic empires' writing as control; Phoenician to Greek literal writing as the citizen's associated milieu; Nora and Minc's comparison of informatics to Sumerian writing (n. 37); the nineteenth-century grammatization of gesture (phonograph, photography, Taylor, n. 38).
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) p. 62: the internet, like the alphabet, printing, machine-tool and TV, is a stage of grammatization that outstrips its actors' intentions ("epokhal double redoubling", n. 4). P. 71: cognitive capitalism is "a stage of the process of grammatization". P. 77: externalization of memory is grammatization. P. 87: the alphabet as grammatization preceding all science (Auroux, n. 40); the third industrial revolution as a passage from mnemotechnical to mnemotechnological societies. The English bibliography wrongly lists Auroux's book under "Christian Fauré".

## Related terms

[tertiary retention](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/tertiary-retention/index.md>) · [hypomnemata](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/hypomnemata/index.md>) · [proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>) · [hyperindustrial society](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/hyperindustrial-society/index.md>) · [transindividuation](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/transindividuation/index.md>) · [pharmakon](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/pharmakon/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ross (2018):** "the primary analytical concept" of the second phase of Stiegler's work. It extends from Palaeolithic "arche-cinema" through gestures in machines and analogue media to binary code, and connects Socrates' pharmakon of writing to Marx's *Grundrisse* ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).
- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** three stages (literal, analogue, digital). The digital is that of hyperindustrial society. The term is borrowed from and "diverted" from Auroux ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Lemmens (2017):** grammatization within general organology; the digital as a new *pharmakon* ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-lemmens-digital-pharmakon-general-intellect-2017/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Labelled interpretation:** the conceptual hinge of the book is that grammatization is *neither* simply loss (Plato, the Frankfurt School) *nor* simply gain (Serres, the "knowledge society" boosters). It is the condition of both, and that is why Ch. 1 says critics of the culture industry lack it.

# Hyperindustrial society (*société hyperindustrielle*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **hyperindustrial society**

## Definition (the book's usage)

Against theories of a "post-industrial" society, Stiegler argues that we live in a **hyper-industrial** epoch. Industrialization now extends beyond material production to **services, culture, cognition and everyday life**: "life itself", including attention and knowledge, is produced and managed industrially. In Ch. 1 this takes the form of **service capitalism**. Services take over activities people once performed themselves and **control the processes by which ways of life are adopted**. The term comes from *De la misère symbolique 1: L'époque hyperindustrielle* (2004).

## Where it appears

- [Introduction](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/01-introduction-what-is-to-be-done/index.md>): "cultural" or "cognitive" capitalism.
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) "The hyperindustrial epoch as service capitalism" (p. 29): there are "no alternatives" to an ever more industrial world. In hyperindustrial society all forms of life become objects of rationalization, investment and service; "de-industrialization" is only a new division of labour. N. 1 refers to *De la misère symbolique 1. L'époque hyperindustrielle* (2004). "Hyperindustrial service societies as the destruction of processes of individuation through the control of processes of adoption" (p. 31).
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) "The re-instrumentation of forms of knowledge and the future of hyperindustrial society" (p. 73): hyperindustrialization is inevitable but has **self-destructive limits**, and calls for a "renaissance of knowledge" and a "sustainable development of spirit".

## Related terms

[proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>) · [grammatization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/grammatization/index.md>) (the digital stage) · [industrial populism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/industrial-populism/index.md>) · [transindividuation](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/transindividuation/index.md>) (adoption as individuation) · [technologies of spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/technologies-of-spirit/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** the **digital** stage of grammatization corresponds to "hyperindustrial society" ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler–Lemmens interview (2010/2011):** the industrialization of the life of the mind; a "new industrial model" rather than an exit from industry ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-lemmens-stiegler-interview-krisis-2011/index.md>)).
- **Ross (2018):** the setting of the "second phase" of the work ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).
- **Hutnyk (2012):** places it in the cognitive-capitalism debate and doubts its novelty ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hutnyk-proletarianisation-2012/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- Against post-industrial theorists (Bell, Touraine), Stiegler's point is that services are *more* industrial, not less. Lotz reads the corollary, that "the future is still to be sought in an industrial mode of production", as a weakness: industrial production is never put in question ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lotz-marx-and-philosophy-2015/index.md>)).
- **Labelled interpretation:** the 2006 notion of "service capitalism" predates platform capitalism, but it describes the same *mechanism* (control of adoption through services). Readers often find it prescient for that reason ([Goodreads](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-goodreads-reader-reviews-2026/index.md>)).

# Hypomnemata (*hypomnèse*, *hypomnémata*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **hypomnemata**

## Definition

Greek: **memory aids**, supports of memory outside the mind. Examples are notebooks, account books, registers and writing in general. In the *Phaedrus*, Plato contrasts ***hypomnesis*** (artificial recall) with ***anamnesis*** (living recollection, the true knowledge of the soul). **Foucault** ("L'écriture de soi", 1983) showed how Stoic and Epicurean *hypomnemata* served as techniques of the self, a "writing of the self". Stiegler joins the two senses. All mnemotechnics, from the alphabet to digital media, are *hypomnemata*. They can support anamnesis and self-constitution or replace them, which makes them *pharmaka*.

## Where it appears

- [Introduction](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/01-introduction-what-is-to-be-done/index.md>) p. 6: hypomnemata supported Foucault's "writing of the self" and also the sophists' control of opinion.
- [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>): ICTs as "a new form of *hypomnemata*" (Foucault, Plato), which "conjure new practices… new social organizations".
- [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>) §4: digital hypomnemata as pharmaka; writing as the pharmakon of reference for Western *savoir-vivre*.
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) n. 3: hypomnemata are artificial memory supports in all their forms, from Australian *tjurunga* and incised prehistoric bones through printing and the Bible to electronic assistants and MP3 players. §3: Chinese characters as "the Asian form of the *hypomnematon*". The future of a society lies in adopting new technologies, "in particular *hypomnemata*".
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) p. 64 (spirit always operates through hypomnemata), p. 73 (Mesopotamian control technologies becoming the hypomnemata of Greek individuation), p. 79 (against Plato: the school as appropriation of the alphabetic hypomnesis).

## Related terms

[tertiary retention](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/tertiary-retention/index.md>) · [grammatization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/grammatization/index.md>) · [pharmakon](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/pharmakon/index.md>) · [technologies of spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/technologies-of-spirit/index.md>) · [otium/negotium](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/otium-negotium/index.md>) · [care](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/care/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** both otium and negotium use hypomnemata ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Holmes (2007):** notes that the Foucault "writing of the self" link is genuinely Ars Industrialis's own ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-holmes-empyre-what-is-to-be-done-2007/index.md>)).
- **Ross (2018):** links Socrates' pharmakon of writing to grammatization ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Labelled interpretation:** the book's core move against Plato is that hypomnesis is the *condition* of anamnesis, not its contrary, which is a Derridean inheritance. Ch. 2 states it in policy terms: build institutions of appropriation.

# Industrial populism (*populisme industriel*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **industrial populism**

## Definition (the book's usage)

Industrial populism is a populism produced **by the organization of the economy**, specifically the culture and program industries and marketing, rather than by political movements. It levels and flatters the lowest common denominator of drives in order to capture audiences and sell their attention. Its emblem is TF1 chief Patrick Le Lay's claim (2004) that what the channel sells Coca-Cola is "available human brain time". The book's subtitle sets the **value of spirit** *against* it. The Introduction defines contemporary "cultural" or "cognitive" capitalism as "before all else the destructive organization of an industrial populism" that uses each technical evolution to turn consciousness into a reflex organ (p. 1).

## Where it appears

- Subtitle; [Introduction](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/01-introduction-what-is-to-be-done/index.md>) p. 1 (definition), pp. 2–3 (Seillière/Le Lay). P. 5: nearly all social life is controlled by the "industry of available brain-time", i.e. industrial populism. P. 7: **financier capitalism** is "the true underwriter of industrial populism".
- [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>) §9.6: media policy against an industrial populism "induced by the drive-based becoming of consumerism".
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) p. 50: industrial populism and tele-cratic television as a process of disindividuation (Berlusconi's "tele-cracy").
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) p. 62: tele-cracy "leads ineluctably to populism". "Enterprises, public power, and industrial populism" (p. 66): evidence from Le Lay; contrast with a knowledge society. P. 69: the model of dissociated milieus "inevitably leads to industrial populism". P. 75: tele-cracy is "the Italian name for industrial populism" (Berlusconi).
- [Tunis motion](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/06-tunis-motion/index.md>) p. 97: TV must become an instrument of knowledge "and no longer the instrument of debasement and of industrial populism".
- Already in Stiegler's *Libération* diary (June 2005): industrial populism produces **desublimation**, which is "the enemy" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-liberation-diary-2005/index.md>)).

## Related terms

[libidinal economy](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/libidinal-economy/index.md>) (drives vs desire) · [symbolic misery](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/symbolic-misery/index.md>) · [spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/spirit/index.md>) · [short-termism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/short-termism/index.md>) · [technologies of spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/technologies-of-spirit/index.md>) · [disenchantment](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/disenchantment/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*, "Populisme industriel et télécratie":** a populism "of a new kind" whose causes are economic. Consumerist societies reach their limits, life becomes drive-based and addictive, and **political populism follows secondarily**. "Telecracy" is mass audiovisual media short-circuiting political transindividuation ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)). In 2013 the association used the concept to analyse the Front National (*Pharmacologie du Front National*).
- **Stiegler, "Uncontrollable Societies" (2006):** ties industrial populism to "available brain time" and to the loss of shame (*aidos*) ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-uncontrollable-societies-nja-2013/index.md>)).
- **Ross (2018):** reads later "industrially-generated populism" and "post-truth" politics as the continuation of this diagnosis ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).
- **Abbinnett (2015):** uses the term as shorthand for the "disorientated life" of consumer culture ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-abbinnett-politics-of-spirit-2015/index.md>)).
- **Context:** the exact wording and source of Le Lay's statement is in [context-le-lay-temps-de-cerveau-2004.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/context-le-lay-temps-de-cerveau-2004/index.md>).

## Disagreements

- The secondary literature **uses the term but rarely analyses it**.
- **Labelled interpretation:** in 2005–06 the concept is *television-centred* (Le Lay, *Star Academy*). Readers such as a Goodreads reviewer note that the remedies are correspondingly TV-focused ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-goodreads-reader-reviews-2026/index.md>)). Its extension to platforms and social media is a later move by Stiegler (2010 Manifesto §4; *The Neganthropocene*).
- The French term differs from the Anglo-American political-science use of "populism". Stiegler's claim is causal: economic organization comes first, political populism second.

# Knowledge vs information (*savoir* / *information*); entropy and negentropy

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **knowledge vs information**

## Definition (the book's usage)

The central distinction of [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>). **Information as a commodity is entropic.** Its value decays with time, as with news and market data. **Knowledge (*savoir*) is negentropic.** It keeps and intensifies its value, is transmitted and reactivated across generations, and "constitutes time". An economy that converts knowledge into information (Lyotard's performativity, "a doing without knowing") therefore carries an internal contradiction. The "knowledge society" risks becoming its opposite, a **reign of ignorance**. *Savoir* covers *savoir-faire* (know-how), *savoir-vivre* (knowing how to live) and theoretical knowledge (*savoirs théoriques*). This three-way division structures the theory of [proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>).

## Where it appears

- [Introduction](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/01-introduction-what-is-to-be-done/index.md>) p. 3: can there be "knowledge without spirit"?
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) §3: capitalism tends "to produce entropy and distaste" and liquidates knowledge (p. 33). N. 12: negentropy fights entropy, "the equalization and indifferentiation of all things", and individuation is essentially negentropic.
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>): adaptation is "deeply entropic" (p. 67). Knowledge is critique and therefore "intrinsically contradictory to adaptation" (p. 72). "Knowledge (*Savoir*) and information" (p. 77) and "Knowledge and memory, or reign of ignorance?" (p. 79): information as commodity is "in its essence entropic"; knowledge is "in its essence negentropic", intensifying (Kant, Thom) and constituting "the time of existence" (pp. 77–79). "Cognitive saturation and 'knowledge management'" (p. 83). Lotz cites p. 23 for knowledge reduced to "controllable, calculative" information, though that page falls in the 2010 Manifesto.
- [Tunis motion](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/06-tunis-motion/index.md>): knowledge is essentially "shared and shareable".

## Related terms

[proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>) · [tertiary retention](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/tertiary-retention/index.md>) · [spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/spirit/index.md>) · [short-termism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/short-termism/index.md>) · [transindividuation](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/transindividuation/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ross (2018):** entropy and negentropy become the axis of Stiegler's late "neganthropological" phase. This book is an early statement of it ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, 2005 Ars Industrialis presentation:** the "cognitive overflow" passage anticipates Ch. 2 ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-arsindustrialis-presentation-tunis-seance-2005/index.md>)).
- **MACBA podcast (2019):** technics can raise or lower entropy ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-macba-sonia-285-stiegler-podcast-2019/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Labelled interpretation:** the thermodynamic vocabulary is asserted rather than derived in Ch. 2. Information theory's sense of entropy (Shannon) differs from the economic "decay of value" the chapter has in mind. Stiegler's later work (*The Neganthropocene*, 2018) tries to make the analogy rigorous through Schrödinger, Lotka and Georgescu-Roegen.

# Libidinal economy (*économie libidinale*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **libidinal economy**

## Definition (the book's usage)

The libidinal economy is the organization and production of **desire**: the channelling of libidinal energy, in Freud's sense of drive energy socialized through **sublimation**, onto objects. Stiegler's thesis is that twentieth-century capitalism made libido its main energy source. Marketing and the culture industries (Bernays) channel desire towards commodities so as to absorb overproduction. That capture ends by **destroying** desire. Desire degrades into **drives** (*pulsions*), attention is short-circuited, and investment in every sense collapses. The Introduction calls this episode of libidinal economy "a destruction of desire" and "a chapter" of Weber's disenchantment (p. 2). The term echoes Lyotard's *Économie libidinale* (1974), but Stiegler's use is Freudian and normative: desire, unlike drive, attaches to singular objects and sustains long-term investment.

## Where it appears

- [Introduction](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/01-introduction-what-is-to-be-done/index.md>) pp. 1–2: Benjamin and Freud missed capitalism's reorganization around the consumer "as a very particular form of libidinal economy".
- [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>): capture of libido as capitalism's energy; its destruction leading "inevitably" to crisis; ruin of sublimation and of the super-ego.
- [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>) §1–3: Bernays; the drive-based consumer and speculator; disinvestment; addiction; contribution "reconstructs a productive economy of desire".
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) pp. 39–43, "capitalism of drives" (p. 39), is the book's fullest statement. Libido is the socialization of sexual-drive energy into sublimatable objects. It projects **consistencies** (love, knowledge, art). The libidinal economy *economizes* by deferring satisfaction (Derrida's *différance*; Freud's pleasure and reality principles, and after 1920 the life and death drives). Libido, "neither oil nor coal", is what makes capital function, and desire is "one of the productions of libido". Capitalism is "an enormous economy of motivation" whose techniques have become counterproductive, turning motives into de-motivation. Exhausting libido destroys *philia* and the "we", making capitalism barbarous. Societies traditionally took care of this energy as *philia*, *eros*, *agape*, *caritas*, *mana* (p. 43).
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) p. 71: talk of "enchantment" is possible because the knowledge economy is first a *libidinal* economy of motives.

## Related terms

[spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/spirit/index.md>) · [industrial populism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/industrial-populism/index.md>) · [short-termism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/short-termism/index.md>) · [symbolic misery](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/symbolic-misery/index.md>) · [care](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/care/index.md>) · [pharmakon](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/pharmakon/index.md>) · [transindividuation](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/transindividuation/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** libido is "socialized and desexualized" drive energy, invested through artefacts (fetishism), which is why it can be industrialized. Unlimited exploitation exhausts it, so a **"renewable" libidinal energy** is needed, an *ecological* problem. *Besetzung* means both libidinal and financial investment ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, "Pharmacology of Desire" (2011):** "libidinal dis-economy"; drive-based capitalism; Le Lay; investment against speculation ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-pharmacology-of-desire-2011/index.md>)).
- **Hansen (2014):** reads the programme as "saving libidinal capitalism", a "short-term economy of the drive" to be replaced by a long-term economy of desire. He calls the project curious, even perverse, for seeking to save capitalism ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hansen-saving-libidinal-capitalism-2014/index.md>)).
- **Abbinnett (2015):** the fall in libidinal energy is "the determining limit of consumer capitalism"; global inequality results from "pathologically disordered forms of libido" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-abbinnett-politics-of-spirit-2015/index.md>)).
- **Lemmens (2017):** accepts the libidinal-exhaustion thesis within a post-autonomist frame ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-lemmens-digital-pharmakon-general-intellect-2017/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Marxist objection** (Lotz; Hutnyk; Manche): putting desire and consumption at the centre makes **labour, capital accumulation and class** "evaporate" from the analysis ([Lotz](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lotz-marx-and-philosophy-2015/index.md>), [Hutnyk](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hutnyk-proletarianisation-2012/index.md>), [Manche](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-manche-proletarianisation-not-capitalism-2021/index.md>)).
- **Arendtian objection** (Roodt): reducing the life of the mind to libido loses what Arendt meant ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-roodt-tydskrif-vir-geesteswetenskappe-2012/index.md>)).
- **Labelled interpretation:** the empirical claim that libidinal energy is being "exhausted" works as a premise in the book rather than a demonstrated finding. Supporters treat it as a structural diagnosis; critics read it as a decline narrative.

# Otium / negotium

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **otium / negotium**

## Definition

Latin terms. ***Negotium*** ("not-leisure") is business: the sphere of subsistence, calculation and exchange. ***Otium*** is studious leisure: time freed from necessity for cultivating oneself and others, reading, writing, contemplation and care of the self. In Greek this is *skholè*, from which "school" derives. Stiegler holds that the two must stay **distinct without being opposed**. Both use *hypomnemata*. Otium aims at "consistences" (ideal objects, the objects of sublimation), and its practices are disciplines or techniques of the self. His charge against service capitalism is that it **folds otium into negotium**: leisure becomes consumption time, and "free" time is sold as available brain time.

## Where it appears

- [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>) p. 13: industrial technologies of spirit, as new hypomnemata like those of the Stoics and Epicureans or of "the Rome in which the Greek *skholè* became the Roman practice of the *otium*", call for new practices. Note 5 cites J.-M. André, *L'Otium dans la vie morale et intellectuelle romaine* (1966). The manifesto also mentions Foucault's "writing of the self" (*hypomnemata* in Stoic and Epicurean schools), which is the practice of otium.
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) develops the related scheme of **subsistence, existence and consistence**. Man cannot merely subsist; he ex-sists (p. 30). Modes of subsistence and existence must support "the other plane", the plane of consistencies, which "do not exist" and must be cared for (pp. 58–60).
- Stiegler's *Libération* diary (June 2005), written in the founding weeks of Ars Industrialis, makes otium explicit. Freedom passes "essentially through *otium*", and otium is equated with **spirit** (sacred or profane), linked to Plutarch's "art of living" and to the journal as a practice of self-writing ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-liberation-diary-2005/index.md>)).

## Related terms

[spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/spirit/index.md>) · [care](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/care/index.md>) · [hypomnemata](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/hypomnemata/index.md>) · [proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>) (loss of savoir-vivre) · [economy of contribution](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/economy-of-contribution/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** negotium is the calculable sphere of business and subsistence; otium is leisure and existence, oriented to consistences and practised through techniques of the self. Service industries short-circuit otium. See also the entries "Skholè" and "Subsister, exister, consister" ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Cohen (2017):** the subsistence/existence/consistence scheme and care of the self (Foucault) ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-cohen-dare-to-care-2017/index.md>)).
- **Abbinnett (2015):** in the contributory economy, freed from "ratio", otium becomes "the global-universal good of prosthetic humanity" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-abbinnett-politics-of-spirit-2015/index.md>)).
- **Rossouw (2015):** the "new otium" as a secularized Christian project ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-rossouw-aestheology-new-otium-2015/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- Abbinnett glosses otium as "**the labour of spirit**". **Labelled interpretation:** this is loose, since otium is precisely *not* labour in the sense of negotium. A charitable reading would say Stiegler distinguishes *work* (*travail*, *œuvre*) from *employment*, so that otium can be "work" without being employment, as in the 2010 Manifesto §9.3.
- Rossouw's theological reading against the secular reading of Ars Industrialis remains open.

# Pharmakon / pharmacology

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **pharmakon**

## Definition

In Plato's *Phaedrus*, writing is offered as a *pharmakon*, a drug that is at once **remedy and poison**. Derrida's "Plato's Pharmacy" (1968) made the ambivalence central. Stiegler generalizes it: **every technics is pharmacological**. It can support or destroy individuation, and which one depends on the practices, institutions and care that surround it. Without a **therapeutic** (*melete*, *epimeleia*: discipline, care, techniques of the self), a pharmakon becomes toxic. "Pharmacology" is the knowledge and politics of this ambivalence.

## Where it appears

- **Explicitly in 2006:** [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) pp. 47–51. Technologies of spirit are "poison and remedy". The *pharmakon* (Plato; Derrida, n. 35), reanalysed in *Mécréance et discrédit 3*, is a question of **socio-therapy**, of care for individuation. Writing in the *Phaedrus* is the citizen's *tekhnē tou biou* and the sophists' weapon. Digital technology is "the *hypomnématon* (the *pharmakon*)" that can reconstitute associated milieus (p. 51). Also, implicitly, [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) p. 79 (anamnesis/hypomnesis).
- **Systematically:** the [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>) §4.1–4.5 and §6 ("hypomnemata are, as pharmaka, remedies as well as poisons"; psychotechnologies must become nootechnologies). De Beer cites French p. 82 for the pharmakon and technologies of spirit ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-debeer-tydskrif-vir-geesteswetenskappe-2012/index.md>)).
- **Chronology:** the *systematic* vocabulary of pharmacology is developed in Stiegler's 2007–2010 work (*What Makes Life Worth Living*, 2010). But the term and the argument are already explicit in Ch. 1 (2006), drawing on *Mécréance et discrédit 3* (2006).

## Related terms

[care](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/care/index.md>) · [hypomnemata](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/hypomnemata/index.md>) · [technologies of spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/technologies-of-spirit/index.md>) · [tertiary retention](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/tertiary-retention/index.md>) · [economy of contribution](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/economy-of-contribution/index.md>) · [proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** remedy, poison *and scapegoat* (the third sense is Derrida's). The pharmakon is both what enables care and what must be cared for. "Positive pharmacology" may still prohibit some pharmaka; the example given is nuclear power ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Abbinnett (2015):** Stiegler extends Derrida's pharmakon beyond writing to all human–technical interfaces. It "sharpens the aporia" of technological society, between capitalized desire and new cathexes of love and spirit ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-abbinnett-politics-of-spirit-2015/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler–Lemmens interview (2010):** a technology is first poisonous and becomes curative only after a second "epochal redoubling" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-lemmens-stiegler-interview-krisis-2011/index.md>)).
- **Lyons (2014):** foregrounds the pharmakon as the root of the book's "philosophy of hope" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lyons-critical-inquiry-2014/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Hutnyk (2012)** turns it back on Stiegler: "stupidity too can be pharmacological", so Stiegler's own decline narrative should be read pharmacologically ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hutnyk-proletarianisation-2012/index.md>)).
- **Manche (2021):** pharmacology combined with an operaist reading of Marx's "Fragment on Machines" yields a teleological view of technology ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-manche-proletarianisation-not-capitalism-2021/index.md>)).
- **Labelled interpretation:** Lyons reads the 2014 *book* through the pharmakon. This fits the 2006 chapters too (pp. 47–51), not only the 2010 Manifesto.

# Proletarianization (*prolétarisation*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **proletarianization**

## Definition (the book's usage)

Proletarianization is the **loss of knowledge** (*savoir*) by individuals when that knowledge is formalized in, and passes into, a technique, machine, apparatus or service. The 2010 Manifesto §6 gives the canonical definition: knowledge "being formalized through a technique, a machine, or an apparatus, can escape the individual". Three waves:

1. **Workers** lose *savoir-faire* (know-how) to machines: Smith and Marx.
2. **Consumers** lose *savoir-vivre* (knowing how to live) to apparatus and services. The TV set "occupying" children is the example, and Ch. 1 §3 has the line "mode de vie" becoming "mode d'emploi" (a way of life becoming a user manual).
3. **Cognitive workers and decision-makers** lose theoretical and critical knowledge to information systems. Greenspan admitted he did not understand the system he managed.

Ch. 1 §3 gives the short form: the proletarian is one who **loses their knowledge**. The producer becomes pure labour power, the consumer pure purchasing power.

## Where it appears

- [Translator's Preface](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/00-translators-preface/index.md>): *savoir-faire*, *savoir-vivre*, double proletarianization.
- Not in the [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>) as a term.
- [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>) §5–6: definition; "disapprenticeship"; free software as **de-proletarianization**.
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>): "The consumer discharged of his existence" (p. 30). §3 (pp. 31–35): generalized proletarianization through service capitalism's control of adoption. "One who has lost his ways of knowing has been proletarianized". The producer loses *savoir-faire* and becomes labour power (*force de travail*); the consumer loses *savoir-vivre*, which becomes a mode of employment, and becomes purchasing power (*pouvoir d'achat*). Fordism generalizes this, masked by making the producer a consumer. P. 51: machines (Taylor), then appliances, exteriorize knowledge into algorithms, giving proletarianization and loss of *savoir-faire*, *savoir-vivre* and contemplation.
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) pp. 71–72: losses of *savoir-faire* and *savoir-vivre* over a few decades, as losses of individuation. P. 74: digital instrumentalization proletarianizes researchers and dissociates cognitive milieus.

## Related terms

[grammatization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/grammatization/index.md>) · [hyperindustrial society](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/hyperindustrial-society/index.md>) · [economy of contribution](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/economy-of-contribution/index.md>) · [associated milieu](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/associated-milieu/index.md>) · [knowledge vs information](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/knowledge-vs-information/index.md>) · [care](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/care/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ross (2018):** "perhaps his fundamental political concept". Socrates is its first thinker; the waves run nineteenth century (work), twentieth (life), twenty-first (theory) ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).
- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** Marx's working class was only the *first* proletarianized class. After 2008 designers and decision-makers are proletarianized by automated systems. The proletarian is "the employee of a dissociated milieu" (Simondon). Proletarianization is "not a fatality" ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, April interview (2011):** plain-language statement of the consumer's loss of *savoir-vivre* ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-april-stiegler-interview-2011/index.md>)).
- **Lotz (2015):** mental life becomes "proletarian" through externalized memory; he notes Stiegler "no longer" speaks Marxist language ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lotz-marx-and-philosophy-2015/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Marxist critics** (Hutnyk 2012; Manche 2021; Lotz): redefining the proletariat by **loss of knowledge** rather than **dispossession and wage-labour** sidelines class, exploitation and accumulation. Manche's title puts it sharply: "The problem is proletarianisation, not capitalism" ([Hutnyk](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hutnyk-proletarianisation-2012/index.md>), [Manche](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-manche-proletarianisation-not-capitalism-2021/index.md>)).
- **Sympathetic readers** (Ross, Lemmens) reply that Stiegler is returning to an earlier sense found in Marx's *Grundrisse* (knowledge absorbed into fixed capital) and in Simondon ([Lemmens](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-lemmens-digital-pharmakon-general-intellect-2017/index.md>)).
- **Labelled interpretation:** the concept explains the book's otherwise surprising politics. If the problem is loss of knowledge rather than ownership, the remedy is de-proletarianization through new practices and instruments, which leaves the question of property in second place.

# Short-termism (*court-termisme*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **short-termism**

## Definition (the book's usage)

Short-termism is the systematic sacrifice of the long term to the short term in investment, management, media and politics. For Stiegler it is not only a financial vice. It is the **temporal form of drive-based behaviour**: the drive wants immediate satisfaction, whereas desire and knowledge are long-circuited and accumulate over time. Shareholder demands for "two-digit returns" (2005 Manifesto), adaptive corporate strategy, audience-ratings TV and speculative finance express one and the same short-termism. Its opposite is **investment**, financial and libidinal (*Besetzung*), and long-term public anticipation.

## Where it appears

- [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>): market criteria favour "short-term financial investments"; shareholders want returns "never below 15%".
- [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>) §1: "neo-liberal short-termism" leads to disinvestment. The speculator is "a capitalist who no longer invests". §5: guarantee the short term in order to reach and **reverse** it in the long term.
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) p. 40: economic actors draw short-term private profit from dissociation and so have no interest in change, "wrong… regarding their own long-term interests". P. 52: financier capitalism dominates and paralyses the long-term initiatives of industrial capitalism.
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) p. 66: Medef's "continuous adaptation" is an entropic vicious circle. Industrial policy for technologies of spirit can only be **long-term**, led by a new public power.
- [Tunis motion](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/06-tunis-motion/index.md>): public and private funds should not seek "short-term returns on investment".

## Related terms

[libidinal economy](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/libidinal-economy/index.md>) · [care](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/care/index.md>) · [knowledge vs information](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/knowledge-vs-information/index.md>) (information's value decays fast; knowledge lasts) · [industrial populism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/industrial-populism/index.md>) · [economy of contribution](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/economy-of-contribution/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire* ("Financiarisation"):** finance as a "commerce of promises". Fully realized short-termism destroys the retentions (knowledge) and protentions (investments) of time (quoting *For a New Critique of Political Economy*, 2009) ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, "Pharmacology of Desire" (2011):** drive-based consumption mirrors speculative disinvestment, with hedge funds and LBOs as examples ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-pharmacology-of-desire-2011/index.md>)).
- **Hansen (2014):** the "short-term economy of the drive" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hansen-saving-libidinal-capitalism-2014/index.md>)).
- **Ross (2018):** the financial crisis as a symptom of increasingly short-term, speculative investment ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- Little disagreement on the diagnosis. The **critics' question** is about agency: who will impose the long term? Stiegler's answer, a "new public power" with industry, is what Lotz and Manche find reformist and Lemmens finds statist ([reception.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/reception/index.md>)).

# Spirit (*esprit*; *la valeur esprit*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **spirit**

## Definition (the book's usage)

*Esprit* is the noetic life of human beings: intelligence, attention, memory, judgement and desire as sublimated. Stiegler treats it as **both psychic and collective**, and as dependent on technical supports. The phrase **"la valeur esprit"**, "the value \[called\] spirit", comes from **Paul Valéry** (1939). Valéry compared spirit to a commodity value, like oil or wheat, whose price can fall, and he saw a "drop in the value of spirit" before the war. The book's wager is that spirit is now the main industrial resource ("after matter, spirit has become the first industrial resource", Tunis motion) *and* the thing being depleted. Spirit in this sense is not religious. The Tunis motion warns against locating spirit only in religion. Nor is it the brain: the Introduction contrasts consciousness, the seat of spirit, with "a brain reduced to an ensemble of neurons".

## Where it appears

- Title and subtitle; [Translator's Preface](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/00-translators-preface/index.md>) (pp. viii–ix: *esprit* versus "spirit").
- [Introduction](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/01-introduction-what-is-to-be-done/index.md>) pp. 1–3: Valéry; is "knowledge without spirit" possible? P. 7: spirit, which always presupposes technologies of spirit, is "a modality of… psychic and collective individuation" (Simondon). Knowledge is "the treasure bequeathed by those who are dead".
- [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>): "technologies of spirit", "industrial ecology of spirit", the "life of the mind/spirit" (Arendt). P. 11: "spirit" is meant also in the sense of the English word "mind", despite its metaphysical and theological baggage.
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>): the **"enslaved spirit… servile spirit, which serves the service societies"** (p. 33; cited by Lotz); capitalism "needs a spirit" (p. 35); "new spiritual devices" (p. 37); capitalism become barbarous is "denuded of spirit" (p. 43); a "debilitated", "rotten" or "servile" spirit cannot found enterprises (p. 46); Weber's spirit of capitalism has been lost through the control of affects (p. 55).
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) title; p. 67 (demotivation as the "drop in the value of spirit", the loss of the "spirit of capitalism"); p. 68 (spirit as the capacity to imagine and concretize alternatives, per Lotz); p. 69 (spirit cannot be adapted; one learns a theorem by re-living its genesis, *methodos*).
- [Tunis motion](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/06-tunis-motion/index.md>): spirit as both "available brain time" and "works of the mind". P. 96: spirit must not be situated "exclusively on the side of the religious"; underinvestment in the value of spirit has fed "regressive and radical spiritualisms". P. 100: reason as "universal *motif* of spirit".

## Related terms

[technologies of spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/technologies-of-spirit/index.md>) · [industrial populism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/industrial-populism/index.md>) · [libidinal economy](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/libidinal-economy/index.md>) (sublimation) · [transindividuation](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/transindividuation/index.md>) · [disenchantment](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/disenchantment/index.md>) (the "spirit of capitalism", after Weber) · [otium/negotium](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/otium-negotium/index.md>) · [knowledge vs information](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/knowledge-vs-information/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** spirit is what brain activity becomes when it turns external things into memory supports. It is the dynamic of technically mediated **transindividuation**, "the 'and'" in Simondon's "psychic *and* collective individuation". When people can no longer *use* the technologies imposed on them, spirit loses its capital and **capitalism loses its spirit** ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, "Uncontrollable Societies" (2006 text):** symbolic misery leads to **spiritual misery** and the fall of the value of spirit. Ross's translator's note on *esprit* as mind and spirit is a useful comparison with Arthur's choice of "spirit" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-uncontrollable-societies-nja-2013/index.md>)).
- **Trevor Arthur:** *esprit* as a synthesis of psychic, social, intellectual and historical life ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-bloomsbury-preview-2014/index.md>)). **Lyons** credits this preface as the best key to the term ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lyons-critical-inquiry-2014/index.md>)).
- **Cohen (2017):** the best gloss of the Valéry genealogy. She links spirit to Stiegler's subsistence/existence/consistence scheme ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-cohen-dare-to-care-2017/index.md>)).
- **Abbinnett (2015):** reads spirit through Derrida's *Of Spirit*. Stiegler shares Derrida's suspicion of Heidegger's *Geist*, but in Abbinnett's reading spirit must pass through epiphylogenetic, written memory ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-abbinnett-politics-of-spirit-2015/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Futural versus memorial.** Abbinnett contests Beardsworth's Nietzschean, "remorselessly futural" reading of Stieglerian spirit and ties it to inherited, technically retained memory.
- **Empty or full?** Lotz calls the positive notion an empty placeholder ("battle against regression", p. 71) ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lotz-marx-and-philosophy-2015/index.md>)).
- **Spirit = libido?** Roodt (Arendtian) argues the manifestos reduce Arendt's "life of the mind" to libido, as a function of economic forces ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-roodt-tydskrif-vir-geesteswetenskappe-2012/index.md>)). De Beer, in the same journal issue, embraces the vocabulary in a quasi-spiritual register ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-debeer-tydskrif-vir-geesteswetenskappe-2012/index.md>)). Rossouw reads re-enchantment as Christianity by other means ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-rossouw-aestheology-new-otium-2015/index.md>)).
- **Labelled interpretation:** the English "spirit" carries religious connotations that *esprit* (also "mind", "wit") does not. This may explain why some English readers hear the book as more spiritualist than French readers do.

# Symbolic misery (*misère symbolique*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **symbolic misery**

## Definition (the book's usage)

Symbolic misery is the loss of individuation that results from losing **participation in the production of symbols**: meanings, works, expressions and affects. The culture industries split producers of symbols from mere consumers. The consumer stops expressing and only receives, and the circuit of symbolic exchange (expression answering expression) breaks. The term comes from Stiegler's *De la misère symbolique* 1–2 (2004–05; English *Symbolic Misery*). In this book it works mostly in the background, as the premise behind **spiritual misery** and the "drop in the value of spirit".

## Where it appears

- Implicit throughout. The [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>) on the destruction of singular objects of desire and symbolic practices.
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) §3: malaise, self-disgust and the insipid world (the *sapere*/*sapide* pun). P. 39: "absolute spiritual misery" (the Nice case, end of 2005). P. 58: a century of aesthetics in the service of production and consumption yields "profound symbolic and spiritual misery".
- [Tunis motion](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/06-tunis-motion/index.md>): "**spiritual misery**" (*misère spirituelle*) striking the industrial world.
- Stiegler's *Libération* diary (June 2005): the ruin of symbolic exchange as "the great symbolic misery in which desire in general collapses" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-liberation-diary-2005/index.md>)).

## Related terms

[libidinal economy](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/libidinal-economy/index.md>) · [industrial populism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/industrial-populism/index.md>) · [proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>) · [transindividuation](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/transindividuation/index.md>) · [associated milieu](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/associated-milieu/index.md>) (dissociated symbolic milieus) · [spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/spirit/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** the loss of individuation through losing participation in symbol production, increasing since the "machinic turn" of culture and politics. Fighting the Front National means fighting symbolic misery, and so industrial populism ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, "Uncontrollable Societies" (2006):** symbolic misery "leads irresistibly to spiritual misery" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-uncontrollable-societies-nja-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, "Pharmacology of Desire" (2011):** the producer/consumer split leaves consumers "de-symbolized" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-pharmacology-of-desire-2011/index.md>)).
- **Ross (2018):** places the *Symbolic Misery* volumes at the start of the political "second phase" to which this book belongs ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Labelled interpretation:** the term is used more than it is explained in this book. A reader new to Stiegler will need *Symbolic Misery* vol. 1, ch. 1–2, to see why aesthetic participation is the model for all participation. The *Libération* diary cites Leroi-Gourhan's "one must participate in order to feel".

# Technologies of spirit (*technologies de l'esprit*); psychotechnologies vs nootechnologies

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **technologies of spirit**

## Definition (the book's usage)

The **2005 Manifesto** coined "technologies of spirit" for the sector formed when digitization makes the **culture industries, program industries, media, telecommunications and cognitive technologies converge**. These technologies are *spiritual* because they work on attention, memory, imagination and desire. They are also ***hypomnemata***. Ars Industrialis is defined as an association "for an industrial politics of technologies of spirit". The 2010 Manifesto sharpens the point into a normative pair. **Psychotechnologies** serve behavioural control (marketing, audience capture). **Nootechnologies** serve the life of the mind and de-proletarianization. The same device can be either.

## Where it appears

- [Introduction](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/01-introduction-what-is-to-be-done/index.md>) p. 3: Ars Industrialis's full name. P. 6: radio, TV, computers and the internet are "spiritual instruments" (Mallarmé on the book).
- [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>) (definition; "industrial ecology of spirit"; control societies).
- [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>) §6: "psychotechnologies… must become nootechnologies, that is, technologies of spirit".
- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>): **"R technologies" are relational technologies** (p. 29; n. 5 cites Rifkin, *The Age of Access*): telecom and broadcast networks, barcodes, chip cards, RFID, wi-fi, Bluetooth, biometrics, nanotechnologies. "R technologies and the new spiritual devices" (p. 37; French "appareils de l'esprit"): in dissociated milieus they serve control, yet they remain technologies of spirit and could support individuation (pp. 37–38). Nora and Minc foresaw the convergence of audiovisual, telecom and computing but not an "industrial politics of technologies of spirit" (pp. 50–51).
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) p. 61 (convergence in the 1990s), p. 73 (control technologies as the condition of future individuation; "technologies of intellect"). Pp. 84–86: Mallarmé's "The Book, a spiritual instrument"; Husserl's "spirit-invested objects"; digital hypomnemata as "new spiritual instruments".
- [Tunis motion](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/06-tunis-motion/index.md>) p. 97: "an industrial politics of technologies of spirit" as the basis for another summit.

## Related terms

[spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/spirit/index.md>) · [hypomnemata](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/hypomnemata/index.md>) · [pharmakon](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/pharmakon/index.md>) · [industrial populism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/industrial-populism/index.md>) · [associated milieu](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/associated-milieu/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire* ("Psychotechnique / nootechnique"):** the opposition is "normative, assumed as such". Psychotechnics act on or against the mind to control it, and nootechnics foster its individuation. The criterion is **reciprocity** (the reader can also write) and long circuits of transindividuation ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, "Within the limits of capitalism…" (c. 2008):** calls for a European industrial politics of technologies of spirit ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-economizing-taking-care-2008/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, 5 Nov 2005 session** on cognitive technologies, knowledge management and design methodology ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-stiegler-technologies-cognitives-2005/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Labelled interpretation:** critics rarely address the term directly. It inherits the debates on [pharmakon](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/pharmakon/index.md>) and on statism ([reception.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/reception/index.md>)).

# Tertiary retention (*rétention tertiaire*)

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **tertiary retention**

## Definition

Tertiary retention is memory **retained outside the living being, in artefacts**: tools, writing, recordings, databases. Husserl distinguished *primary* retention (the just-past held in the present of perception, as when a note's sound lingers in a melody) from *secondary* retention (recollection). Stiegler adds **tertiary** retention, the technical, "epiphylogenetic" memory that both stores the past and **conditions** the other two. What we can perceive and remember is overdetermined by the recording and selection technologies of an epoch. Marketing and the program industries operate by controlling tertiary retentions, and through them **protentions** (expectations and desires).

## Where it appears

The term appears **explicitly** in the Introduction's n. 2 (p. 101): the psychic apparatus distributes itself into prostheses and technical apparatuses that support "what I have elsewhere called tertiary retentions", which Ars Industrialis calls hypomnemata. Elsewhere the idea runs under other names:

- [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>) and [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>): **hypomnemata** and "mnemotechnologies".
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) "Knowledge (*Savoir*) and information" (p. 77) and "Knowledge and memory, or reign of ignorance?" (p. 79). Memory is externalized from the human origin; living memory exceeds its "retentional finitude" by exteriorization (p. 79); the **mnemotechnical → mnemotechnological** transition. "Instruments of knowledge and the criteria of selection" (p. 87): memory as retention is **selection**, and industrializing it defines new criteria of selection (p. 88; Lotz: memory and imagination become objects of investment).

## Related terms

[hypomnemata](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/hypomnemata/index.md>) · [grammatization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/grammatization/index.md>) · [knowledge vs information](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/knowledge-vs-information/index.md>) · [pharmakon](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/pharmakon/index.md>) · [proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire* ("Attention, rétention, protention"):** tertiary retentions are hypomnesic sediments in artefacts that **overdetermine** secondary retentions, which in turn overdetermine primary ones ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Ross (2018):** marketing and cultural tertiary retentions aim to control **protention**, which leads to "hypercontrol" and then "uncontrollability" ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, "Pharmacology of Desire" (2011):** money is itself a tertiary retention and protention ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-pharmacology-of-desire-2011/index.md>)).
- **Manche (2021):** a clear standard exposition; the concept is introduced in *Technics and Time* 3 ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-manche-proletarianisation-not-capitalism-2021/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Labelled interpretation:** Ch. 2's anti-Platonic argument (writing is memory's condition, not its death) is the clearest application in the book. Its target is Michel Serres's view that externalizing memory to machines frees us for pure knowledge. For Stiegler, there is no knowledge outside its retentional supports.

# Individuation, transindividuation, disindividuation

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/GLOSSARY/index.md>) › **transindividuation**

## Definition

From **Simondon** (*L'individuation psychique et collective*). **Individuation** is the never-finished process by which an individual becomes who it is. It is always at once **psychic** (an "I") and **collective** (a "we"). Stiegler adds a third, **technical** strand, because individuation passes through artefacts and memory supports. **Transindividuation** is the co-individuation of "I"s that produces a "we": shared meanings, knowledges and institutions, metastabilized in symbols and techniques. **Disindividuation** is the breakdown of this process. It happens when psychotechnologies **short-circuit** transindividuation: they impose ready-made identifications, saturate attention, or split producers of meaning from consumers.

## Where it appears

- [Translator's Preface](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/00-translators-preface/index.md>): individuation ("one becomes who he is") and transindividuation ("we become who we are").
