- [Ch. 1](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>) p. 30: service industries short-circuit transindividuation; n. 7: individuation is not individualization. §3 (pp. 31–33): **individuation is adoption**, and service capitalism destroys individuation by controlling adoption (primary and secondary identification). P. 34: Simondon (*IPC* p. 18) on the individual as an element in a vaster individuation, with **language** as the model of participatory psychic and collective individuation. P. 47: "Grammatization and individuation". P. 57 (quoted by Lotz): hyper-solicitation of attention "short-circuits transindividuation", causing dis-identification and **disindividuation**. N. 49: the double sense of "disaffected".
- [Ch. 2](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>) p. 71: spirit is a matter of motives, so of psychic and collective individuation. P. 81: "**The risk of disindividuation** as the growth of ignorance rather than knowledge". Individuation is always psychic *and* collective; knowledge exists only as shared and public.

## Related terms

[spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/spirit/index.md>) (as the "and" of psychic and collective) · [associated milieu](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/associated-milieu/index.md>) · [grammatization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/grammatization/index.md>) · [symbolic misery](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/symbolic-misery/index.md>) · [proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>) · [hyperindustrial society](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/concepts/hyperindustrial-society/index.md>)

## How secondary sources gloss it

- **Ars Industrialis *Vocabulaire*:** spirit is the dynamic of technically mediated transindividuation ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)).
- **Stiegler, "Pharmacology of Desire" (2011):** psychotechnologies short-circuit transindividuation ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-pharmacology-of-desire-2011/index.md>)).
- **Hui &amp; Halpin (2013):** "collective individuation" as a design goal for social networks, against individualist user models ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hui-halpin-collective-individuation-2013/index.md>)).
- **Ross (2018):** care and knowledge "metastabilize" transindividuation ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)).
- **Lotz (2015)** quotes p. 57 as the book's central formulation of the existential crisis ([source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lotz-marx-and-philosophy-2015/index.md>)).

## Disagreements

- **Labelled interpretation:** Stiegler's adaptation thesis (individuation = **adoption**, from *Technics and Time 3*) is a distinctive addition to Simondon. It turns the theory into a theory of culture and marketing: whoever shapes adoption shapes individuation.

## The French edition, and FR/EN differences

1. **The 2010 Manifesto is not in the 2006 French first edition.** The Introduction's n. 17 (p. 102) says that at the time of the French publication only the 2005 Manifesto existed, and that the 2010 Manifesto was added in the English edition. It was written in 2010 (it refers to the 2007–2010 crisis and Facebook's 500 million users in July 2010). The English edition (2014) therefore **adds** it. Its vocabulary of *pharmakon*, care and the economy of contribution belongs to Stiegler's 2008–2010 work and is **later than the chapters**. Readers should not read those concepts back into Chs. 1–2.
2. **The 2005 Manifesto is in the French edition.** French catalogues note "Contient le Manifeste d'Ars Industrialis".
3. **Authorship is presented differently.** The French cover reads "Bernard Stiegler et Ars Industrialis". The English title page names Stiegler alone, though the translator's preface speaks of "Stiegler and co.". The two chapters are Stiegler's own texts. The manifestos and motion are signed collectively (Collins, Crépon, Perret, B. Stiegler, C. Stiegler).
4. **French pagination anchor.** Ch. 1 §3 ("Les sociétés hyperindustrielles de services comme destruction des processus d'individuation par le contrôle des processus d'adoption") is at French pp. 42–47 (English pp. 31–33). That implies roughly 1.4 French pages per English page.
5. **French Ch. 1 section headings** in retailer and catalogue listings: "capitalisme de services", "Les sociétés hyperindustrielles de services comme destruction des processus d'individuation par le contrôle des processus d'adoption", "technologies R" with "appareils de l'esprit" (the English has "new spiritual devices").
6. **The French back cover** is a compressed version of the Introduction's opening (Valéry 1939; 45% radio; "temps de cerveau disponible"; "un cerveau sans conscience"; Medef 2005; "ce livre propose de le prendre au mot").
7. **French pagination of the 2005 Manifesto: pp. 27–35** (per the bibliography of de Beer 2012, [source](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-debeer-tydskrif-vir-geesteswetenskappe-2012/index.md>)). The French front part (Introduction, "Que faire ?") therefore runs to about p. 26, and Ch. 1 begins soon after p. 35.
8. **Opening text titled "Que faire ?"**: attested by a 2007 English summary ([Holmes](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-holmes-empyre-what-is-to-be-done-2007/index.md>)), which is consistent with the English "What Is to Be Done?".
9. **Editions:** BnF FRBNF40245952 (Flammarion 2006, 172 pp.); Champs paperback reissue, 3 Oct 2008, 176 pp. (EAN 978-2-08-121784-3); e-book 2013. See [sources/review-bnf-catalogue-records-2006.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-bnf-catalogue-records-2006/index.md>).
10. **An earlier partial English translation exists.** Two sections were translated by Stephen Barker in *New Formations* (2012): "Grammatisation and Individuation Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow" (= Ch. 1, p. 47) and "The Risk of Disindividuation as the Increase of Ignorance Rather Than Knowledge" (= Ch. 2, p. 81). See [sources/review-barker-new-formations-2012.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-barker-new-formations-2012/index.md>).

**French section headings, as given in retailer listings** (Eyrolles for the 2008 Champs printing; Furet du Nord):

| French heading (as listed) | English equivalent | Observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "**Refonder la société**" | Ch. 1 "The Re-Foundation of Society" | the French uses a verb ("re-found society") |
| "**Le sursaut : entreprendre autrement**" | "The jumpstart (*le sursaut*): starting over again" (p. 44) | "entreprendre autrement" = "undertaking / doing business otherwise", whereas the English has "starting over again" |
| "**Faire la révolution du capitalisme**" | "Making the revolution of capitalism" (p. 51) | matches |
| "**A european way of life**" (in English in the French original) | "A European way of life" (p. 53) | Stiegler used the English phrase; the translation keeps it |
| "**Le plan qui m'enchante**" | "The plane that enchants me" (p. 58) | correctly rendered: the section is about the *plane* of consistencies or motifs ("the plane of motifs… the plane of enchantment", p. 58), French *plan* |
| "**Contre le règne de l'ignorance – investir dans l'augmentation de la valeur esprit**" | Ch. 2 title (p. 61) | matches ("increase" = *augmentation*) |

- The English section on the *sursaut* turns on *entreprendre*: "UNDERTAKE A FOUNDATION (ENTREPRENDRE DE FONDER)" (p. 46). The French subtitle "entreprendre autrement" plays on *entreprendre*/*entreprise* (business), which "starting over again" does not carry.
- **The French edition prints the Tunis motion, at FR p. 163** (Ch. 2, n. 6).
- **The bibliography (pp. 113–114) contains an error:** *La Révolution technologique de la grammatisation* (Mardaga, 1993) is listed under "Fauré, Christian". The book is by **Sylvain Auroux**, and Ch. 2 n. 40 cites it correctly by title.
- Ch. 2 n. 20 shows why the French edition is dedicated to Laurence Parisot. Stiegler saw her succession to Seillière at Medef as giving "some hope" for civic responsibility among French employers.

## Genealogy of the parts (where each text comes from)

| Part | Origin | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Introduction | Written for the book (2006); draws on Stiegler's June 2005 *Libération* diary and the Sept 2005 Colline talk §3 | Shared Medef/Kessler/Seillière/Le Lay material; French back cover |
| 2005 Manifesto | Founding text of Ars Industrialis (spring 2005) | arsindustrialis.org node/1472 |
| 2010 Manifesto | Ars Industrialis, 2010 | arsindustrialis.org/manifesto-2010 |
| Ch. 1 | Stiegler: "reformulation and elaboration" of a paper from one of the first two Ars Industrialis working sessions after 18 June 2005 (Introduction, p. 8), updated to spring 2006 (it cites events of April 2006) | Introduction p. 8; notes to *Mécréance et discrédit* 2–3 and *La Télécratie contre la démocratie* (2006) |
| Ch. 2 | **Revised and expanded version of Stiegler's talk at the Ars Industrialis session of 24 Sept 2005 (Théâtre de la Colline)**, given to prepare the Tunis motion | Section headings match one-to-one and in order: [sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-colline-2005.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-colline-2005/index.md>) |
| Tunis motion | Adopted a few days before the Tunis summit; *Libération* (14 Nov 2005) published **excerpts**, and the book prints the **complete text** (Introduction, p. 9) | arsindustrialis.org node/2126 (the *Libération* version) |

## Reading order note

The book's order is not the order of composition. Composition ran 2005 Manifesto (spring 2005) → Ch. 2 (Sept 2005) → Tunis motion (Nov 2005) → Ch. 1 and Introduction (2006) → 2010 Manifesto. Chronologically, the book is the founding dossier of Ars Industrialis, framed by a 2006 introduction and updated in 2014 with the 2010 manifesto.

## 5\. All source files by type

See [sources/EVALUATION.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/EVALUATION/index.md>) for ratings. File-name prefixes: `primary-` (book texts), `primary-parallel-` (Stiegler's contemporaneous texts), `review-` (accounts of the book), `lit-` (secondary literature), `glossary-`, `media-` (lectures, podcasts, blogs, wikis, reader reviews), `context-` (events the book presupposes).

# Reception and critique

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › **Reception** · sources rated in [sources/EVALUATION.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/EVALUATION/index.md>)

*Everything in this file is evaluation, by reviewers, critics or (where marked) us. The summaries in `chapters/` and `concepts/` deliberately leave it out.*

## 1\. Publication history and audience

- **2006 (FR).** Published by Flammarion in October as a short, cheap book co-signed with the new association. It was one of four Stiegler books that year, alongside *Mécréance et discrédit 2–3* and *La Télécratie contre la démocratie*, and it was the most programmatic of them. Reissued in Flammarion's Champs paperback series in 2008, which is the source of the "2008" date that some sites give ([Babelio](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-babelio-reader-reviews-2024/index.md>), [catalogue records](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-bnf-catalogue-records-2006/index.md>)).
- **French reception** is thin. It consists of a bookseller note ([Charybde](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-hugues-charybde27-2024/index.md>)), a short web review that finds the book "peu accessible aux non-initiés" ([Cherrier](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-cherrier-lelitteraire-2012/index.md>)), and reader pages. A 2007 review appeared in *Spirale*. Ars Industrialis's own sessions (2005–07) were the book's main French context ([context](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/context-ars-industrialis-association/index.md>)).
- **Early English circulation** came before the translation, via tactical-media and net-art milieus ([Holmes 2007](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-holmes-empyre-what-is-to-be-done-2007/index.md>)), and via two sections translated by Stephen Barker in *New Formations* (2012) ([Barker](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-barker-new-formations-2012/index.md>)).
- **South African reception (2012).** A pair of Afrikaans articles in *Tydskrif vir Geesteswetenskappe*: de Beer's enthusiastic review-article and Roodt's Arendtian critique of the manifestos ([de Beer](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-debeer-tydskrif-vir-geesteswetenskappe-2012/index.md>), [Roodt](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-roodt-tydskrif-vir-geesteswetenskappe-2012/index.md>)).
- **2014 English edition.** Reviewed by Patrick Lyons in *Critical Inquiry* and Christian Lotz in *Marx &amp; Philosophy Review of Books* (2015). ([Lyons](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lyons-critical-inquiry-2014/index.md>), [Lotz](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/review-lotz-marx-and-philosophy-2015/index.md>)).

## 2\. Lines of critique

### 2.1 "Abstract diagnosis, empty remedy"

**Lotz:** the positive notion of spirit is expressed through "empty placeholders" ("battle against regression", "conquest of the best over the worst", p. 71). The only concrete example of cooperative knowledge tools is Wikipedia (p. 87). **Lyons** agrees that the book offers few concrete answers, though he reads it as a "philosophy of hope". Goodreads readers repeat the verdict: strong diagnosis, abstract remedies ([Goodreads](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-goodreads-reader-reviews-2026/index.md>)). - *Possible response (labelled interpretation):* the book does contain sectoral proposals. These are Ch. 2's "practical consequences" (pp. 91–94: specific instruments for research and education, new editorial functions, delinearized audiovisual objects, societies of authors and readers) and the 2010 Manifesto's seven policy planks (six in the web draft). What is missing is less concreteness than an account of **political agency**: who carries the programme against whom.

### 2.2 The Marxist objection: proletarianization without class

**Lotz:** control of labour "evaporates" into control of consumption. The production/consumption dialectic and the role of money and capital go unanalysed, and the framework is Kantian, Enlightenment and reformist social-democratic. **Hutnyk (2012)** and **Manche (2021)** generalize the point. Redefining proletarianization as loss of knowledge sidelines exploitation and accumulation. It yields "good capitalism vs bad capitalism", and the contributory economy risks self-exploitation and co-optation ([Hutnyk](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hutnyk-proletarianisation-2012/index.md>), [Manche](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-manche-proletarianisation-not-capitalism-2021/index.md>)). - *Primary evidence relevant to the dispute:* the book's own section titles ("Making the revolution of capitalism"; "The jumpstart"); Stiegler's 2005 call for an "enlightened capitalism" ([Libération](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-stiegler-liberation-diary-2005/index.md>)); the Tunis motion's "new spirit of capitalism"; and Stiegler in 2010 bracketing the question of whether the new model will still be capitalism ([Lemmens interview](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/primary-parallel-lemmens-stiegler-interview-krisis-2011/index.md>)). The reformist reading is textually well grounded. Whether reformism is a fault is a judgement of framework.

### 2.3 Statism and Europeanism

The manifestos and motion call for a "new form of public power" with industry, and for a European industrial policy (Beffa, Lisbon). **Lemmens (2017)** finds this statist, and doubts it can be squared with the decentralized contributory model ([Lemmens](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-lemmens-digital-pharmakon-general-intellect-2017/index.md>)). **Lotz** notes the "politics of decentralization" (p. 63) but sees no movement to carry it.

### 2.4 Spirit and its genealogy

- **Roodt (Arendtian):** the 2005 Manifesto invokes Arendt's *Life of the Mind*, but by treating mind as libido and as a function of economic forces it loses Arendt's distinction between thinking and doing.
- **De Beer:** embraces the spirit vocabulary in a quasi-spiritual, Heideggerian register.
- **Abbinnett:** a Derridean reading. Spirit must pass through technical memory, against Beardsworth's "futural" reading ([Abbinnett](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-abbinnett-politics-of-spirit-2015/index.md>)).
- **Rossouw:** re-enchantment and the "new otium" as Christianity by other means ([Rossouw](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-rossouw-aestheology-new-otium-2015/index.md>)).
- **Cohen:** the Valéry genealogy; care as Foucauldian *epimeleia* ([Cohen](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-cohen-dare-to-care-2017/index.md>)).

### 2.5 Media-theory reception

**Hansen** finds it "curious", even "perverse", that the programme seeks to *save* libidinal capitalism by re-enchanting it ([Hansen](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-hansen-saving-libidinal-capitalism-2014/index.md>)). **Lyons** reads the 2014 book through the pharmakon. **Lotz** credits it with extending culture-industry critique from content to technological systems.

### 2.6 Decline narrative and empirical claims

**Hutnyk** reads Stiegler as a conservative "decline" theorist and contests his claims about television and children. The house glossary's claims about screens and synaptogenesis are asserted without discussion ([glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/glossary-arsindustrialis-vocabulaire-2013/index.md>)). Hutnyk also turns the pharmakon on Stiegler: "stupidity too can be pharmacological".

### 2.7 Style

Almost all readers note difficulty: "excessive use of technical terminology" (Lotz), associative prose and shorthand (Lyons), "peu accessible" (Cherrier). A minority call it "tonique" (Charybde).

## 3\. The author's own revision

In *The Neganthropocene* (2018), Stiegler cites this book as his analysis of Simondon's associated milieus in the digital age. He also concedes that the algorithmic web has become "a systemically dissociating milieu, because it is hyper-proletarianizing". That partly withdraws the 2005–2010 hope that digital networks are intrinsically contributory ([Ross file](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/lit-ross-neganthropocene-introduction-2018/index.md>)). By 2019 the programme had become a "contributory economy" against entropy, the Neganthropocene ([MACBA podcast](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-macba-sonia-285-stiegler-podcast-2019/index.md>)).

## 4\. Afterlife

- **Ars Industrialis** ran sessions, working groups, the *Vocabulaire* and the pharmakon.fr school. In 2020 it changed its statutes, becoming the "Association des Amis de la Génération Thunberg" ([context](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/context-ars-industrialis-association/index.md>)).
- **"Available brain time"** became a French classroom topic, via documentary rather than this book ([fiche](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-plandetudes-fiche-temps-de-cerveau-2010/index.md>)).
- Recent readers find the book prescient about attention economies and AI ([Goodreads](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/sources/media-goodreads-reader-reviews-2026/index.md>)).

## 5\. Errors in circulation

| Claim | Where | Correct |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Book co-authored with three people | EN Wikipedia | Five founders sign the collective texts: George Collins, Marc Crépon, Catherine Perret, Bernard Stiegler, Caroline Stiegler |
| Catherine Malabou a co-founder | some search summaries | Not among the founders in any primary source |
| Motion adopted "at" the Tunis Summit; book includes "an account of the organisation's summit in Tunis" | Lyons; bookseller blurbs | A motion adopted a few days before the summit; *Libération* (14 Nov 2005) printed excerpts, and the book prints the complete text (Introduction, p. 9) |
| Stiegler at Centre Pompidou in June 2005 | P2P Foundation wiki | Still IRCAM director; Pompidou from 1 Jan 2006 |
| Published 2008 | some sites | 2006 first edition; 2008 is the Champs paperback |
| The 2010 Manifesto is part of *Réenchanter le monde* | implied by the EN packaging | Added in the English edition only |
| Same book as Maffesoli's *Le Réenchantement du monde* (2007) or Landy &amp; Saler (2009) | search conflation | Unrelated books |

## 6\. What the book's own text says on these debates

*Evaluation, labelled.* The text of the book bears directly on several of the disputes above.

- **Reformism is explicit, with a hedge.** Capitalism "to this day does not have a credible alternative" (Introduction, p. 6). The aim is to make "the revolution of a capitalism that is on the road to collapse" together with "revolutionary capitalists", likened to the French bourgeoisie of the late eighteenth century (p. 53). Public opinion should back *industrial* capitalism against *financier* capitalism (p. 7). This supports Lotz, Hutnyk and Manche on the reformist reading. Yet Stiegler also writes of a new spirit of capitalism "while waiting for the replacement of the latter by another form of society" (p. 37), and of no future "of capitalism, or a beyond of capitalism, which is certainly not eternal" (p. 60). His position is therefore post-capitalist in horizon and reformist in strategy, not simply pro-capitalist.
- **"Only Wikipedia" is too strong.** Lotz says Wikipedia is the book's only example of cooperative knowledge instruments. Chapter 1 already rests its alternative on open-source software, Linux and the IP network as an associated milieu (pp. 36–37), and the 2010 Manifesto adds free software, smart grids and AMAP.
- **"Abstract remedy" is partly answered.** Chapter 1 specifies the agents (a new European public power; enterprising citizens), the model (the economy of contribution) and the danger (financier capitalism and tele-cracy). Its political agency remains thin, as Lotz says: there is no account of how the public power is to be built against the interests that profit from dissociation, interests the chapter itself identifies (p. 40).
- **The labour objection.** Lotz says labour control "evaporates". Chapter 1 does address labour: Taylorism as the grammatization of gesture (n. 38); de-industrialization as offshoring to "very poorly remunerated workers, if not… slaves" (p. 29); and the proletarianized producer turned consumer under Fordism (p. 35). But it subordinates exploitation of labour to the loss of knowledge and the exhaustion of libido, which is just what the Marxist critics object to.
- **The decline narrative.** Chapter 1's evidence for "spiritual misery" is largely anecdotal and drawn from the press: a Nice crime, Skyblogs, the Durn and Brunerie cases, the November 2005 riots, an Inserm study on attention disorders (pp. 39, 57–58). This bears out Hutnyk's methodological complaint, though it is consistent with the book's genre as an engaged manifesto.
- **The pharmakon reading** (Lyons) is supported by the 2006 text itself (pp. 47–51), not just by the 2010 Manifesto.
- **Lotz's page citations are accurate.** His references to pp. 1–4, 6–7, 23–24, 33 ("enslaved spirit"), 57 (short-circuiting transindividuation) and 58 ("lost the feeling of existing") all match the text.
- **Property.** The complete motion (p. 95) calls knowledge a common good that "does not belong to anyone" and accepts only *temporary* limits from intellectual property. That is a sharper challenge to property relations than the Marxist reviews allow. Ch. 2 still frames the aim as "the reconstitution of a capitalist future" (p. 67).
- **State and the US model.** The motion praises American federal industrial strategy (the internet, the FCC, the State with universities and the military) as a model for Europe (pp. 98–99). This supports Lemmens's charge of statism, but it is a strategic, not a nationalist, statism.
- **Concreteness.** Ch. 2 names specific projects (INA 1997, IRCAM, IRI, the 1989–92 computer-assisted-reading prototype, the 1996 Nord-Pas-de-Calais report). The "abstract remedy" charge fits the philosophical framing better than the policy content.
- **Hindsight.** The judgement that Lisbon "will have been a total failure" (p. 91) may be a later revision for the English edition.

## 7\. Open questions

These are open questions the sources leave undecided. They are posed neutrally and are not answered here:

- Does the *knowledge/information* (negentropy/entropy) distinction hold up outside its thermodynamic metaphor?
- Is "loss of knowledge" a deeper or a narrower definition of proletarianization than Marx's?
- Can an "industrial politics of spirit" be carried by public power and industry, as the book proposes, or does it require a social movement, as its critics say?
- How should the 2006 hope for digital "new spiritual devices" be read after platform capitalism and the author's own 2018 revision?

# Optional

# Evaluation of sources

[Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/index.md>) › **Source evaluation** · see also [reception.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/reception/index.md>)

Each source in `sources/` is rated on five criteria:

- **Accuracy:** against the book itself (see [STRUCTURE.md](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/STRUCTURE/index.md>)).
- **Coverage:** which parts of the book it treats: P = Preface, I = Introduction, M05 / M10 = Manifestos, C1 / C2 = Chapters, T = Tunis motion.
- **Depth:** how far the source goes, from 1 (notice) to 5 (sustained analysis).
- **Stance:** interpretive bias.
- **Reliability:** high / medium / low.

The files themselves hold the condensed account and fuller notes.

## A. Primary texts and primary-parallel texts (authorial)

These are not "accounts" of the book; they are the book's own texts or Stiegler's contemporaneous versions of its arguments. They anchor the accuracy judgements below.
